controls_available: Full input uses physical mouse dragging from a four-slot inventory material to a selected process machine, the three-input assembler, or the delivery bay; machine CYCLE buttons, RESET BENCH, one recipe replay, and CERTIFY DEVICE remain available after the recipe seals.

Difficulty 1 generates branch lengths [1,1,1], two selected process machines, four inventory slots, three process transforms plus final assembly, initial recipe exposure of 9000-9800 ms, replay exposure of 6000-6400 ms, memory charge 3, replay cost 1, and one replay.
The shared task settings are a 1200 ms observation window with 8 frames per observation and 180 seconds of play time.
autonomous_processes: The initial recipe shutter closes on a generated fixed timer in the 9000-9800 ms range; while it is open, route, cycle, reset, replay, and certification controls are gated by recipeSealed.
The optional replay shutter closes on a generated fixed timer in the 6000-6400 ms range; it restores recipe visibility and then only enables later controls when it seals.
Each accepted machine or assembly cycle shows four fixed readout pulses at 0, 95, 190, and 285 ms and commits its output at 410 ms while the bench is busy.
grouped_control_modes: Full physical_drag transfers from an inventory slot to a process station, assembler, or delivery bay.
machine_cycle_button for each selected process station and for final assembly.
Replay button, reset button, and certification console.

clause_i.reason: Across generated recipes, the required next station is not determined by the agent's prior actions or task times. Identical action histories can precede different sealed branch sequences, so an observation-free fixed route cannot choose every correct machine.

clause_ii.reason: After the shutter seals, the bounded recent window does not retain the multi-branch recipe needed for later route choices. The replay control is a separate action that reopens the recipe; it does not make the post-seal route itself recoverable from one bounded recent window.

clause_iii.reason: The recipe and replay shutters close after fixed waits and closure only enables controls. A machine cycle is already committed by the prior click; its fixed 410 ms busy period blocks controls and then installs the next item. No available outcome-affecting action becomes strictly less effective because of this autonomous change.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The visible shutter transition and the visible four-pulse cycle/output transition are the only autonomous task changes. Neither provides a common expiring control opportunity: shutter closure archives information and enables later actions, while cycle completion settles an action that was already taken and does not degrade a still-available action. Therefore no common D, positive Delta, and bounded window witnesses all three clauses.

pre_run.reason: A successful instance requires repeated material transfers, a separate cycle action for each transformation and assembly, and a final delivery transfer before certification. The source has no autonomous phase that can complete the route after outcome-affecting actions stop.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 profile: [1,1,1] branches, two process stations, four-slot inventory, and fixed recipe/replay timing and memory parameters.
Full is physical drag, simplified is click-to-place, and the shared observation window is 1200 ms with 8 frames and 180 seconds of play time.
The generator materializes the selected profile, samples branch lengths and selected machines, and creates a random station sequence.
Generated recipe and replay windows, memory settings, inventory, and active stations are placed in public and hidden state.
Recipe and replay shutters use timers, seal the recipe, and gate replay until the recipe is sealed.
Full mode accepts a physical drag only after the recipe is sealed and records its trajectory.
A cycle sets busy, emits fixed four-phase readouts, commits output after 410 ms, and then clears busy.
The UI disables cycle, replay, reset, and certification controls while the recipe is open or the bench is busy.
The cycling gauge and recipe shutter are visibly represented, without adding a task-state process beyond the JavaScript timers.
The grader enforces shutter timing, mode-specific transfer transcripts, fixed-duration cycles, and final lineage outcome; it does not grade a continuously expiring opportunity.
The verifier loads the exported UI result and delegates the outcome to the independent grader.
The normal solver waits for sealing, optionally replays, then performs repeated transfers and cycle clicks before delivery and certification.
